subject: Soft-break ladder + phased true-up proposal for Polaris Health
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Peters <alex.peters@polarishealth.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 5 Dec 2029 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Soft-break ladder + phased true-up proposal for Polaris Health

Alex —

Thanks for taking the call yesterday. Per our discussion I put together a concise proposal for a per-token ladder that blends predictability with flexibility for seasonal spikes. Key ideas in this email (and attached spreadsheet):

- Soft-break tiers: instead of a hard step change at a breakpoint, the lower rate partially applies for the first month after crossing. This reduces invoice shock for high-velocity windows.
- Marginal vs blended: we recommend marginal math for internal clarity but offer a blended effective-rate view for your finance team to reconcile budgeting. The spreadsheet shows both.
- Phased true-up (90 days): we propose a 90-day rolling true-up window to smooth sudden growth; credits applied progressively over the window.
- Velocity credits: short-term credits to offset one-time spikes during onboarding/batch runs. 3-month cap.

Attachments: pricing_model.xlsx (tabbed: marginal_vs_blend, monthly_sim), Polaris_SOW_v2.pdf (SOW stub).

I tried to keep the offer simple: a 3-tier ladder with soft-breaks at 500M and 2B tokens, marginal pricing by default, and an optional effective-rate billing view for monthly statements.

If that looks sensible I can:
- Share a worked invoice example for Jan–Mar based on the sample traffic you shared;
- Draft a slim amendment to the SOW capturing the phased true-up language;
- Book a 30-min sync with finance/legal if you want to walk through the math.

Suggested next step: Wed 11 Dec, 10:00–10:30 PT — does that work?

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Sales Director, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0123
From: Alex Peters <alex.peters@polarishealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.inference>
Cc: procurement@polarishealth.com, Kunal Shah <kunal.shah@polarishealth.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Dec 2029 11:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Soft-break ladder + phased true-up proposal for Polaris Health

Soojin —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the spreadsheet. A few follow-ups from procurement/finance after a quick read:

1) Can you show a side-by-side invoice example where we hit 1.8B tokens in Month 2 and 2.3B in Month 3? We need to see both marginal and blended effective-rate numbers for our CFO.
2) How are velocity credits triggered? Is it an opt-in for onboarding or automatic? We prefer deterministic triggers.
3) For the phased true-up: what happens if usage drops below the previous tier within the 90-day window? Will we owe retroactive reconciliation?
4) Any SLA/latency exceptions tied to soft-breaks or fallback to a cheaper model variant during peaks? We may want automated fallback to a sustained cheaper model if latency or capacity becomes constrained.

Also: procurement asked for a short clause to appear in the SOW that limits cumulative credits to X% of committed spend — can you propose language?

We can do Wed 11 Dec 10:00 PT. I’ll invite a finance rep (Kunal) and our security partner on the thread if needed.

Thanks,
Alex
Director, ML Platforms
Polaris Health
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.inference>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 5 Dec 2029 13:08:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Soft-break ladder + phased true-up proposal for Polaris Health (internal)

Looping in Laura for legal/finance language. Quick notes for the call and what to send Alex before Wed: 

- Invoice sample: I can run the Jan–Mar scenario in pricing_model.xlsx and export a worked invoice (will attach trueup-example.csv). That will show marginal vs blended rows and an 'effective rate' line for CFO.
- Velocity credits: propose deterministic triggers: onboarding = first 60 days after go-live; sustained spike = >200% of 4-week rolling avg for 7 consecutive days. Credits auto-apply but are capped at 5% of monthly committed spend (we can surface the cap in the SOW).
- Phased true-up drop scenario: suggest 'downside protection' language — if usage falls back below the higher tier within the 90-day window, we perform a lookback and apply only net positive credits; we do not invoice retroactive penalties to the customer, but true-up will reduce future credits. Keep it customer-friendly to avoid churn.
- SLA fallback: we support model-variant fallback by policy; that is operational rather than pricing. Propose a sentence that model fallback does not adjust committed token counts but may change per-token cost for served tokens if a cheaper model is used during fallback windows.

I’ll attach the CSV and a short SOW paragraph for procurement to review.

-Rafael
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Peters <alex.peters@polarishealth.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.inference>, procurement@polarishealth.com
Date: Thu, 5 Dec 2029 16:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Soft-break ladder + phased true-up proposal for Polaris Health

Alex —

Appreciate the clear questions. Short answers and next steps below (I included Rafael and Laura for detail/contract language):

Q1 — Worked invoice: attached in pricing_model.xlsx and exported in trueup-example.csv. Bottom line: when Month 2 = 1.8B and Month 3 = 2.3B, marginal billing results in a ~12% month-3 delta vs blended; the CFO view (effective rate) is included as a separate column.

Q2 — Velocity credits: deterministic triggers as Rafael suggested (onboarding window + >200% spike rule). Credits are auto-applied and capped at 5% of the monthly committed spend; we will display them on the invoice as a line item for transparency.

Q3 — Phased true-up on drops: we won’t retroactively invoice for drops. True-up reduces future credits rather than charging back; language: "In the event of a downward adjustment within the true-up window, Redwood will offset future credits proportionally and will not invoice the Customer for retroactive usage penalties." (Laura: please flag any legal concerns).

Q4 — SLA/fallback: operational fallback to a cheaper model can be enabled; tokens served by fallback count toward committed usage but pricing for those tokens follows the model variant price. We can include a policy appendix documenting fallback behavior.

SOW clause proposal (draft):
"Cumulative credits applied under the Velocity Credit and Phased True-up provisions shall not exceed 5% of the Customer's committed monthly spend in any contractual month. Redwood will itemize credits on monthly invoices and provide a 90-day rolling reconciliation report upon request."

Next steps:
- Rafael will upload the exported invoice example (trueup-example.csv) and I’ll push a slim SOW paragraph into Polaris_SOW_v2.pdf.
- Confirm Wed 11 Dec 10:00 PT for a 30-min sync (invitation pending).

If anything else you'd like pre-reads on the call please tell me — we can add a short one-pager on blended vs marginal math.

Best,
